tagline: Highway 2 through oil towns that boomed, busted and stayed put.
intro: Highway 2 starts at the Texas line, swings around the tip of Caddo Lake, crosses the Red River into Bossier Parish and keeps east through Plain Dealing toward Lake Claiborne. Plain Dealing holds the Louisiana heat record, 114 degrees on an August day in 1936.

The byway's subject is the boom and the bust, in oil and gas, timber, farming and the rest. Parts of the road pass graveyards of old oilfield equipment that died when the oil went bust, and new oil and gas works going up for the next boom.

moments.title: Caddo Lake
moments.text: A lake of flooded cypress where Gulf Refining finished the world's first over-water oil platform in 1911, and derricks soon stood all across the water.

moments.title: Germantown Colony
moments.text: North of Minden, two hewn-log buildings remain from a German religious commune of about thirty-five people who held all property in common from 1836 to 1871.

moments.title: Homer
moments.text: Oil came in at Homer in 1921. Across from the 1860 courthouse, the old Hotel Claiborne now keeps a museum that claims the oldest compressed cotton bale in the country.
